references.name: Faces
references.summary: Select world-cardinal planar faces consistently across within-component feature operations.
references.use_when: Use Faces with Shape.on(), Shape.shell() and Edges.from_faces() so placement and modify features share one surface vocabulary.
references.limits: TOP/BOTTOM are +/-Z, LEFT/RIGHT are -/+X and FRONT/BACK are -/+Y. Native topology selection uses the largest planar face with the requested normal. Component assembly attachment uses Anchor instead.

references.name: Anchor
references.summary: Select component attachment references and cardinal directions.
references.use_when: Use cardinal or corner anchors to attach reusable component occurrences, or combine cardinal values to identify Box edges/corners.
references.limits: Anchor is the assembly/alignment vocabulary. Within-component feature placement normally uses Faces instead. INNER_BOTTOM has no direction vector and therefore cannot be used as a cardinal selector.

references.name: Axis
references.summary: Select one of the native principal X, Y or Z axes.
references.use_when: Use Axis for primitive orientation and supported patterns, for example Cylinder(..., axis=Axis.X) or a linear Hole pattern along Axis.Y.
references.limits: Axis is a principal-axis selector, not an attachment reference and not an extrusion Direction.

references.name: Depth
references.summary: Choose a supported feature-depth policy.
references.use_when: Use Depth.THROUGH_ALL for features such as Hole that should pass completely through their target instead of using a fixed distance.
references.limits: THROUGH_ALL is currently the only named depth policy.

references.name: Edges
references.summary: Select edge topology for supported fillet and chamfer feature operations.
references.use_when: Use Edges.from_faces(...) for the complete boundary of one or more named Faces. Existing Edges.VERTICAL, from_profile() and from_vertices() remain available for their established selection contracts.
references.limits: from_faces() resolves native SolidCraft topology at replay time. from_profile() currently supports sides="both"; from_vertices() requires named Polygon2D vertices.

references.name: Shape
references.summary: Store Forge geometry and feature operations before SolidCraft executes them.
references.use_when: Shape values are normally returned by constructors such as Box(), Cylinder(), Hole() and Sketch.extrude(), then transformed or combined with the supported Shape methods/operators.
references.limits: Shape is only Forge's description of the model. SolidCraft owns the final BRep and feature history; users normally do not instantiate Shape(kind, data) directly.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Forge node type. Public constructors set this; normal model code should not invent kind values.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: Data stored for that node type. Public constructors and methods build this payload.

references.name: component
references.summary: Declare one reusable physical component definition.
references.use_when: Decorate a model class whose build() result represents one reusable physical part. Child defaults stay fixed unless explicitly published with include=. Parent Parameter/Expression inputs remain symbolic.
references.limits: build() must produce one Shape when reused as a component.

parameters.name: cls
parameters.description: Model class whose build() returns one physical part. Omit when using @component(...) as a decorator factory.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Child default parameters to publish. Use names, "*", or a mapping for renamed shared parameters.

references.name: assembly
references.summary: Declare a reusable class that composes component occurrences.
references.use_when: Decorate a class when the class itself represents a reusable assembly or subassembly built from component occurrences and their relationships.
references.limits: build() must return a component occurrence or Assembly. The decorator does not itself create grouping or attachment relationships; those come from the objects returned by build().

parameters.name: cls
parameters.description: Model class whose build() returns a component occurrence or Assembly.

references.name: Occurrence.copy
references.summary: Create another occurrence of the same reusable definition.
references.use_when: Reuse one component definition for another physical occurrence.
references.limits: Attachment state is occurrence-specific and is not copied.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Optional explicit Forge name for the new occurrence.

parameters.name: placement
parameters.description: Optional absolute Placement for the new occurrence. When omitted, the source placement is inherited.

references.name: Occurrence.attach
references.summary: Create a rigid, planar or explicit native revolute relationship from this occurrence to another component.
references.use_when: Placement should be expressed semantically between component references, including a bounded hinge/revolute axis, rather than as a calculated global XYZ pose.
references.limits: Omit kind to retain automatic rigid/planar behavior. kind="revolute" currently requires zero in-plane offset and accepts fixed finite degree value/limits. The target must be another component occurrence; AnchorFrame/AnchorTopology cover specific joint datums. as_built=True remains rigid-only.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: Parent component occurrence to attach to.

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description: Attachment reference on target. Defaults to Anchor.RIGHT.

parameters.name: child
parameters.description: Attachment reference on this occurrence. Defaults to Anchor.LEFT.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: In-plane (u, v) offset on the parent attachment plane, in mm. Defaults to (0, 0); revolute currently requires zero.

parameters.name: gap
parameters.description: Separation along the parent anchor normal, in mm. Defaults to 0.

parameters.name: angle
parameters.description: Optional joint-frame rotation in degrees.

parameters.name: as_built
parameters.description: When True, keep existing poses and create an as-built rigid joint.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Optional explicit relationship kind. Currently supports "revolute"; omit for automatic rigid/planar behavior.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Initial revolute angle in degrees. Defaults to 0 when kind="revolute".

parameters.name: limits
parameters.description: Optional (minimum, maximum) revolute angular limits in degrees.

parameters.name: flip
parameters.description: Native joint-origin flip for a revolute relationship. Defaults to False.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Optional non-empty native joint name.

references.example: moving = moving.attach(fixed, parent="hinge_axis", child="hinge_axis", kind="revolute", value=60, limits=(0, 180), name="Hinge")
references.signature: Occurrence.attach(self, target, *, parent=<Anchor.RIGHT: 'right'>, child=<Anchor.LEFT: 'left'>, offset=(0, 0), gap=0, angle=None, as_built=False, kind=None, value=None, limits=None, flip=False, name=None)

references.name: Occurrence.group

references.use_when: Give one occurrence a useful native browser/subassembly parent.
references.limits: Grouping changes hierarchy only. It does not align, attach or otherwise create a mechanical relationship. One occurrence cannot belong to several different groups.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Native group/subassembly name.

references.name: DrawingView
references.summary: Describe explicit paper placement, optional scale and qualified native display style for one standard drawing view.
references.use_when: Place a front, top, right or isometric native SolidCraft view at a deliberate paper coordinate, optionally override its scale, and use the qualified shaded style for a pictorial view.
references.limits: at is paper-space millimetres. scale is SolidCraft scale text such as '1:1'. visual_style currently qualifies only 'shaded'; omit it for the normal native line presentation. DrawingView configures one of the standard native views rather than creating an arbitrary camera.

parameters.name: description

parameters.name: designer

parameters.name: checker

references.name: Sketch.rectangular_pattern
references.summary: Repeat a profile or earlier Sketch result with a native rectangular pattern.
references.use_when: Repeat one Circle, Slot or other supported profile without drawing every copy separately. The returned Sketch result represents the source plus its copies and may be passed to mirror() or another supported Sketch operation.
references.limits: The operation must be authored inside the active Sketch. Current native qualification covers attached Sketch(on=...) use. The two counts may create at most 500 instances in total. Per-instance suppression is not supported. SolidCraft 0.42 stores the curves selected by a mirror when that mirror is created. If a pattern later creates extra curves after its count changes, those new curves are not added to that existing mirror automatically.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: A profile already in this Sketch, or a result returned by rectangular_pattern() or mirror() in the same Sketch.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Number of instances in the first direction, including the original. Use a whole number from 1 to 500; a dimensionless Parameter may remain editable in SolidCraft.

parameters.name: spacing
parameters.description: Distance between instances in the first direction, in mm. A length Parameter may remain editable in SolidCraft.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: First sketch-local direction: Axis.X, Axis.Y or a fixed non-zero (x, y) vector. Defaults to Axis.X.

parameters.name: count2
parameters.description: Number of instances in the second direction, including the original. Use a whole number from 1 to 500. Defaults to 1.

parameters.name: spacing2
parameters.description: Optional distance between instances in the second direction, in mm. When omitted, SolidCraft uses the first spacing.

parameters.name: direction2
parameters.description: Optional second sketch-local direction: Axis.X, Axis.Y or a fixed non-zero (x, y) vector. When omitted, SolidCraft uses the direction perpendicular to the first.

parameters.name: alignment
parameters.description: Position of the original along the first direction: "left", "center" or "right". Defaults to "right".

parameters.name: alignment2
parameters.description: Position of the original along the second direction: "left", "center" or "right". Defaults to "right".

parameters.name: reversed
parameters.description: Reverse placement along the first direction. Defaults to False.

parameters.name: reversed2
parameters.description: Reverse placement along the second direction. Defaults to False.

references.example:
with Sketch(name="Holes", on=board, parent=Anchor.TOP) as sketch:
circle = Circle2D(d=8)
row = sketch.rectangular_pattern(
circle, count=4, spacing=25, direction=Axis.X
)
with Sketch(name="Slots", on=board, parent=Anchor.TOP) as sketch:
slot = SlotCenterToCenter2D((0, 0), (20, 0), 8)
pair = sketch.rectangular_pattern(
slot, count=2, spacing=30, direction=Axis.Y
)
references.signature: Sketch.rectangular_pattern(self, source, *, count, spacing, direction=<Axis.X: 'X'>, count2=1, spacing2=None, direction2=None, alignment='right', alignment2='right', reversed=False, reversed2=False)

references.name: Sketch.mirror
references.summary: Mirror a profile or earlier Sketch result over the sketch X or Y axis.
references.use_when: Create symmetric sketch geometry from a Circle, Slot, pattern result or earlier mirror result. The returned Sketch result contains the mirrored copies and may be used by a later supported Sketch operation.
references.limits: The operation must be authored inside the active Sketch. Current native qualification covers attached Sketch(on=...) use. Only the sketch X and Y origin axes are supported. SolidCraft 0.42 stores the curves selected when the mirror is created. If an upstream pattern later creates extra curves after its count changes, those new curves are not added to that existing mirror automatically.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: A profile already in this Sketch, or a result returned by rectangular_pattern() or mirror() in the same Sketch.

parameters.name: axis
parameters.description: Mirror axis. Use Axis.X, Axis.Y, "x" or "y".

references.example:
with Sketch(name="Holes", on=board, parent=Anchor.TOP) as sketch:
circle = Circle2D(d=8)
sketch.mirror(circle, axis=Axis.Y)
with Sketch(name="Slots", on=board, parent=Anchor.TOP) as sketch:
slot = SlotCenterToCenter2D((0, 0), (20, 0), 8)
pair = sketch.rectangular_pattern(
slot, count=2, spacing=30, direction=Axis.X
)
sketch.mirror(pair, axis=Axis.X)

references.name: parameters-positioning
references.summary: Keep dimensions symbolic and express readable offsets or parent-bound positions.

members.name: Parameter
members.summary: Represent one named editable CAD dimension.
members.use_when: Keep a value symbolic so generated SolidCraft commands can retain an editable dependency instead of baking in the current Python number.
members.limits: value must be finite. Normal public lower-case model fields are usually promoted to parameters automatically, so explicit Parameter() is mainly useful in lower-level or assembly code.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: SolidCraft parameter name. It must be a valid Python identifier.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Current numeric value of the parameter.

members.name: Placement
members.summary: Absolute pose of one occurrence in its parent coordinate frame.
members.use_when: Declare the pose of a component occurrence at creation or copy time.
members.limits: Placement is occurrence creation state, not a relative move action. Coordinates, rotation axis and angle must evaluate to finite values.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: Absolute X position in mm. May be numeric, Parameter or Expression.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: Absolute Y position in mm. May be numeric, Parameter or Expression.

parameters.name: z
parameters.description: Absolute Z position in mm. May be numeric, Parameter or Expression.

parameters.name: rotation
parameters.description: Optional (axis, degrees) absolute rotation. axis may be X/Y/Z, Axis, or a non-zero XYZ vector.

members.signature: Placement(x: object = 0, y: object = 0, z: object = 0, rotation: tuple[object, object] | None = None) -> None

members.name: X
members.summary: Axis token with MIN, CENTER and MAX parent-bound placement selectors.
members.use_when: Public X, Y and Z tokens let feature offsets refer to a parent bound, for example X.MIN + 10 or Y.MAX - 10, without hard-coding the current global coordinate.
members.limits: These X/Y/Z tokens are bound selectors, not Axis.X/Y/Z primitive-axis enum values.

members.name: Y

members.use_when: Public X, Y and Z tokens let feature offsets refer to a parent bound, for example X.MIN + 10 or Y.MAX - 10, without hard-coding the current global coordinate.
members.limits: These X/Y/Z tokens are bound selectors, not Axis.X/Y/Z primitive-axis enum values.

members.name: Z

members.limits: These X/Y/Z tokens are bound selectors, not Axis.X/Y/Z primitive-axis enum values.

members.name: half
members.summary: Return half of a numeric or symbolic CAD dimension.
members.use_when: Keep midpoint-style arithmetic readable without converting a symbolic CAD dimension to a concrete Python value.
members.limits: Equivalent to value / 2; the input must support that operation.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Numeric, Parameter or Expression value to divide by two.

members.name: midpoint
members.summary: Return the midpoint between two numeric or symbolic dimensions.
members.use_when: Express a centre position while preserving symbolic CAD dependencies.
members.limits: Equivalent to (start + end) / 2; inputs must support symbolic arithmetic.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: First numeric or symbolic coordinate/dimension.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: Second numeric or symbolic coordinate/dimension.

members.name: cadmath
members.summary: Namespace for native symbolic CAD math.
members.use_when: Derived editable dimensions need min/max, roots, quantization or atan while retaining Parameter dependencies.
members.limits: Use cadmath.min/max/sqrt/abs/round/floor/atan. It is native CAD-expression authoring, not a general symbolic algebra package.

members.name: pv
members.summary: Return the concrete Python value of a symbolic CAD dimension.
members.use_when: Python itself genuinely needs a number for validation or control flow.
members.limits: Calling pv() intentionally removes the symbolic dependency at that point. Geometry and placement should normally keep Parameter/Expression objects symbolic so SolidCraft remains editable and associative.

parameters.name: dim
parameters.description: Numeric value, Parameter or Expression to read as a Python float.

members.example:
if pv(clearance) < 0:
raise ValueError("clearance must not be negative")

references.name: attachment-references
references.summary: Use richer local or topology-backed datums when a standard Anchor is not enough.

members.name: AnchorFrame
members.summary: Describe one local attachment point and orientation.
members.use_when: A standard face or corner Anchor is not enough and the mounting datum needs its own local origin plus orientation. A reusable component may expose named AnchorFrame values from anchors(), or an assembly may pass one directly to attach().
members.limits: z and x must be non-zero and must not be parallel. Direct frames on explicitly rotated occurrences have limited support as documented by the assembly guide.

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description: Component-local XYZ attachment point in mm. Defaults to (0, 0, 0).

parameters.name: z
parameters.description: Attachment-normal direction as an XYZ vector or Anchor. Defaults to Anchor.UP.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: Local X/clocking direction as an XYZ vector or Anchor. Defaults to Anchor.RIGHT.

members.signature: AnchorFrame(origin: tuple[float, float, float] = (0.0, 0.0, 0.0), z: tuple[float, float, float] | scpf.core.Anchor = <Anchor.TOP: 'top'>, x: tuple[float, float, float] | scpf.core.Anchor = <Anchor.RIGHT: 'right'>) -> None

members.name: AnchorTopology
members.summary: Describe an attachment datum that follows native SolidCraft topology.
members.use_when: A relationship should follow a particular edge, adjacent planar face and optionally one endpoint as dimensions change, rather than freezing one XYZ coordinate.
members.limits: edge and on are native selection pick points. Current Forge support focuses on planar-face edges and non-rotated occurrences. z and x, when both supplied, must not be parallel.

parameters.name: edge
parameters.description: XYZ pick point on the target edge, in component-local mm.

parameters.name: on
parameters.description: XYZ pick point on the adjacent planar face, in component-local mm.

parameters.name: corner
parameters.description: Optional XYZ endpoint/corner pick in component-local mm.

parameters.name: z
parameters.description: Optional non-zero XYZ attachment-normal override.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: Optional non-zero XYZ clocking-direction override.

members.signature: AnchorTopology(edge: tuple[float, float, float], on: tuple[float, float, float], corner: tuple[float, float, float] | None = None, z: tuple[float, float, float] | None = None, x: tuple[float, float, float] | None = None) -> None

members.name: compile_model
members.summary: Compile one Shape tree to a native SolidCraft command document.
members.use_when: Lower-level tooling already has a final Shape object and needs the JSON command plan without executing a model source file.
members.limits: The final value must be a Shape. Normal user workflows usually call the scpf runner/CLI instead.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: Final Shape tree to compile.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Model/body name used for generated SolidCraft commands. It must be a valid identifier.

members.name: run_script
members.summary: Execute a trusted SCPF model source file and return its command document.
members.use_when: Programmatic tooling needs the same model-loading/root-selection and compilation behaviour as the SCPF CLI.
members.limits: The source is executed as trusted Python. A file must either end in an explicit root model call or define exactly one unambiguous public model class with build().

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Path to the trusted Python model source file.

references.name: diagnostics
references.summary: Public diagnostics for invalid model intent and lost symbolic parameter dependencies.

members.name: ModelError
members.summary: Report unsupported or invalid CAD model intent.
members.use_when: Catch Forge compilation/model validation failures separately from normal Python argument errors when integrating the lower-level compiler API.
members.limits: User model code normally fixes the underlying model instead of handling this exception as a recoverable geometry result.

members.name: ModelParameterWarning
members.summary: Warn that an editable model parameter lost a native CAD dependency.
members.use_when: Tooling wants to detect parameters that became concrete Python values or are only partly associative in the generated SolidCraft model.
members.limits: This is a warning category, not an exception. The preferred fix is to preserve the symbolic relationship or mark an intentional build-time input with a leading underscore.

references.name: Shape.with_appearance
references.summary: Assign one fixed display color to the final body without changing physical material semantics.
references.use_when: A model should open with a specific visual color while material, density and BOM behavior remain unchanged.
references.limits: This first contract accepts one opaque fixed #RRGGBB color and applies it to the final body. Call it after geometry operations.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: Display color as a #RRGGBB hex string.

references.name: Configure
references.summary: Author a native editable configuration table on the final design.
references.use_when: Define editable native configuration rows rather than Python-only variants.
references.limits: Rows modify native configuration columns only; Configure does not branch or rebuild Python model structure per row.

parameters.name: design
parameters.description: Final Shape, component occurrence or Assembly.

parameters.name: active
parameters.description: Name of initially active row.

parameters.name: columns
parameters.description: Ordered Param and Suppress columns.

parameters.name: rows
parameters.description: Ordered mapping of row names to cell sequences.

references.name: Param
references.summary: Select an existing native model parameter for a configuration column.
references.use_when: Prefer Param(self.parameter) inside build() so configuration intent follows the actual symbolic model parameter; a parameter name string remains accepted when a direct object is unavailable.
references.limits: Configuration intent is authored generically and must lower to a native editable SolidCraft table; unsupported intent fails explicitly.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Native parameter name or Parameter object.

references.name: Suppress
references.summary: Select one applied Forge feature for native suppression.
references.use_when: Define editable native configuration rows rather than Python-only variants.
references.limits: Configuration intent is authored generically and must lower to a native editable SolidCraft table; unsupported intent fails explicitly.

parameters.name: feature
